title: Budget-aware eval orchestrator for catalog + tenant pin changes with priority sampling
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: When a model in the catalog or a customer-pinned model is upgraded we need to run automated quality checks, but naive fan-out to run full eval suites is expensive and can overwhelm compute budgets. This ticket scopes a policy-driven eval orchestrator that triggers on pin/upgrade events and enforces budget-aware, tenant-prioritized, differential sampling and staged fanout to minimize cost while maintaining high-fidelity regression detection. The goal is to replace ad-hoc eval runs with a predictable, auditable pipeline that balances signal quality and unit cost.
background_and_context: Customers and catalog maintainers pin model versions frequently; several recent near-regressions (see incident notes below) were only caught after manual evaluations, causing delayed rollbacks.
Existing automation triggers full preflight evals for small tenants and selective smoke checks for large tenants. This is inconsistent and results in variable detection lead time and cost.
We must support both catalog-level promotions (affecting many tenants) and tenant-scoped pin updates (single-tenant), and treat them differently in sampling and budget allocation.
acceptance_criteria: A policy engine exists to classify pin events into priority buckets: critical (catalog hotfix), high (catalog minor upgrade), normal (tenant pin), and low (catalog doc minor).
For each bucket, a sampling policy defines: initial sample size, staged expansion thresholds, and cost cap (tokens / GPU-hours).
Tenant-priority weights are applied for multi-tenant catalog promotions so customers with higher SLA or recent regressions receive earlier/full checks.

Orchestrator executes a staged fanout: 1) lightweight smoke (synthetic prompts) within 15 minutes, 2) targeted fidelity probes on high-impact prompt sets within 2 hours, 3) optional full eval if differential metrics exceed thresholds.

Budget guard triggers throttling or auto-cancel of optional stages when observed cost >= configured cap or cluster pressure is high; observed throttling must be visible in Console and via webhook events.
All runs are recorded with metadata (event id, pin source, tenant list, sampling seed, policy version) and surfaced in the Eval dashboard with diff visualizations and alerting rules.

Rollout is tested with canary: first 5% of catalog promotions and 10 internal tenants for tenant pins; telemetry shows stable cost within 10% of projection and detection rate at or above baseline for seeded regressions.
Documentation and runbook for on-call: how to interpret eval results, abort flows, and rollback recommendations are published and linked in ticket.
technical_requirements: Event ingestion hook for pin change events (catalog and tenant) with normalized payloads (source, old_version, new_version, tenant_ids, traffic_profile).
Policy engine microservice with versioned policies and a simple DSL or JSON schema to express sample_size, staged_steps, cost_cap, tenant_weights.
Sampler service that can pull tenant traffic profiles and produce deterministic sample shards given a sampling seed.
Integration with existing eval harness and probe runner (ENG-42177) so stages map to concrete test suites: smoke, fidelity-probes, full-eval.
Cost accounting hooks: estimate tokens/GPU-hours per sample and real-time reporting back to orchestrator for throttling decisions.
Console UI additions: a 'Pin Event' timeline with status, budget usage, sampled tenants list, and links to per-tenant diffs and PRs.
Webhook and alert integration to notify platform owners when a stage detects a regression exceeding thresholds or when budget caps are hit.
success_metrics: Mean time from pin event to first actionable regression alert <= 30 minutes for >80% of critical catalog events.
Cost per catalog promotion evaluation reduced by at least 40% vs running full-fidelity evals for all tenants.
False negative rate for seeded regressions remains <= baseline (±5%).
Operator time spent triaging pin-related regressions reduced by 30% within first month of rollout.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive sampling misses regressions. Mitigation: staged expansion and conservative thresholds in initial rollout; include seeded regressions in canary to validate detection.
Risk: Budget throttling delays detection on high-impact sellers. Mitigation: tenant-weighting and SLA-exempt buckets for high-priority customers.
Risk: Orchestrator adds latency to promotions. Mitigation: smoke stage is lightweight and returns immediate pass/fail; policy supports synchronous bypass for emergency hotfixes.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal): implement policy engine + sampler + smoke stage integration; run on internal catalog promotions for 2 weeks.
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5% of catalog promotions and 10 selected tenants; include seeded regressions to validate sensitivity. Monitor cost and detection metrics daily.
Phase 2 (wider): enable default policy for all tenant pins and 50% of catalog promotions; introduce tenant-weighted prioritization and UI components in Console.
Phase 3 (GA): enable for all pin events, expose policy controls (editable) to platform admins; ship docs and runbooks.
implementation_notes: Prototype policy schema: {bucket, sample_seed, initial_sample_count, staged_steps:[{name, suite, expand_if_metric_gt, max_cost}], cost_cap}. We'll keep as JSON schema stored in Git.
Sampling algorithm: deterministic hashing over tenant_id + sample_seed ensures reproducibility and consistent shard membership across re-runs.
Cost estimator will use historical per-sample token distribution (from Console metrics) with a safety margin; orchestrator uses real-time counters to decide throttle.
Prefer reusing ENG-42177 probe runner for stage execution; small adapter work needed to accept orchestrator job spec.
